# SK1022 — Precompute a constant character search set

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A private static readonly character array is used only by framework span search operations.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 7.2 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

SearchValues precomputes a reusable search strategy. The fix changes existing cached storage rather than allocating SearchValues at each call, and requires available framework factory and search overloads.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
static readonly char[] Separators = " ,;|\t".ToCharArray(); // span.IndexOfAny(Separators)
```

Write:

```csharp
static readonly System.Buffers.SearchValues<char> Separators = System.Buffers.SearchValues.Create(" ,;|\t");
```

## When it does not fire

Initial coverage is char arrays with 4 or more distinct constant characters and at most 256 characters, used exclusively as the values argument of framework span IndexOfAny, IndexOfAnyExcept, ContainsAny or ContainsAnyExcept. Array/collection initializers and constant-string ToCharArray are supported. String.IndexOfAny, byte sets, mutable/escaping storage, partial types, directives, comments, expression trees and other-file source constants are excluded. Other static initializers and static constructors are excluded to avoid reentrant initialization differences. Requires metadata SearchValues and compatible search overloads; small sets are left alone. Measure performance for the target workload. Reflection on the private field is outside the proof.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK1022.severity`
